features.name: Real Claude, for free
features.description: Speak or type and get answers from the genuine Claude — not a local imitation — at no per-message cost.
features.notes: claude_cli backend drives headless `claude -p` on the owner's subscription token (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), not the metered API

features.name: Claude speaks in a male voice
features.description: Every reply is spoken aloud in a warm male voice; printed text stays unchanged.
features.notes: edge-tts en-US-AndrewNeural; Windows SAPI 'David' offline fallback; pt-BR-AntonioNeural ready but deferred

features.name: Talk instead of type
features.description: the owner speaks into his microphone; his speech is transcribed locally and answered out loud.
features.notes: faster-whisper STT runs on-device; push-to-talk, clipboard paste, or hands-free loop

features.name: Keeps his name straight
features.description: Asked who he is, the assistant always answers 'Claude' — never 'Andrew' (the voice timbre).
features.notes: Identity rule enforced in the system prompt and project rules

features.name: Claude vs Ronald
features.description: Switch between the real Claude and a local stand-in named Ronald, by config or just by saying a name in chat.
features.notes: brain.py dual-brain router; 'Claude ...' wakes the real me, 'Ronald, take a break' brings me back

features.name: Ronald never pretends to be Claude
features.description: The local helper is told to admit he is Ronald, has no access to the owner's data, and must never invent meetings or project facts.
features.notes: Anti-hallucination system prompt — the fix for a 2026-06-21 incident where the local model impersonated Claude

features.name: Hard-set lock
features.description: Pin the active brain so name-switching is ignored — keeps the real Claude locked in until the owner unlocks it.
features.notes: config brains.locked=true (current state); web toggle UI on :8720

features.name: Honest 'not connected' fallback
features.description: If the real Claude can't be reached and Ronald is disabled, the assistant says so plainly instead of faking an answer.
features.notes: fallback_to_local=false; never silently hands a real-Claude question to the local model

features.name: Claude on LINE
features.description: Chat with Claude on LINE by text or voice note; he replies with both text and a spoken voice note.
features.notes: line_bot.py on :8721, public via Cloudflare tunnel claudevoice.quiddityinnovations.com; 24/7 service

features.name: Claude on Telegram
features.description: Same two-way text-and-voice conversation on Telegram, with per-chat memory.
features.notes: telegram_bot.py outbound long-poll (no open port); 24/7 service

features.name: Owner controls
features.description: the owner's direct messages are binding; he can pause the bot, allow/block guests, set a standing directive, or clear memory.
features.notes: /stop /resume /guests /directive /reset /whoami /video — owner LINE DM only

features.name: Guest guardrails
features.description: Friends chatting with the bot get warm small talk only — no project access, no work tasks, pointed to their own Claude account.
features.notes: Separate guest system prompt; ignores attempts to override the rules

features.name: Talking-avatar video
features.description: Claude can reply with a short video message — his avatar image plus his voice.
features.notes: /video command works (still avatar + voice); HD lip-sync is opt-in/heavy; auto-video stays off until async push is verified

features.name: Smart reply modality
features.description: The system decides per reply whether to send text, voice, or video — short conversational answers get voice, long/code answers stay text.
features.notes: modality.py rules engine, shared design for future bots

features.name: A room Claude hosts
features.description: A Zoom-style room where Claude greets people, sees who's present, facilitates, and speaks — open it in a browser.
features.notes: meeting_server.py on :8722; starts daily 08:00 via scheduled task; loopback-only today

features.name: Humans and AI agents together
features.description: People join from a browser and other AI agents join over a connection; everyone shares one live transcript and each gets a distinct voice.
features.notes: WebSocket room; humans' speech transcribed, everyone's text spoken — a text/voice junction box; agent_join.py template

features.name: Polite turn-taking
features.description: Claude answers when addressed and may courteously interject on a strong point, but stays quiet when one participant addresses another.
features.notes: find_addressee + maybe_interject; agents answer only when named, to stop bot-to-bot loops

features.name: Meeting minutes on demand
features.description: Turn the live transcript into structured minutes (summary, discussion, decisions, action items) and download them as a Word document.
features.notes: POST /minutes -> .docx in data/minutes; factual, never invents attendees

features.name: 24/7 across reboots
features.description: The channels and public tunnel run as Windows services, so Claude stays reachable even when no one is logged in or working.
features.notes: QI_ClaudeVoiceLine, QI_ClaudeVoiceTelegram, QI_ClaudeVoiceTunnel, QI_ClaudeVoiceControl via NSSM

features.name: Hourly self-health check
features.description: Every hour the system probes the real-Claude path end to end and alerts the owner if it goes degraded.
features.notes: bridge_health.py + QI_ClaudeVoiceBridgeCheck task; Tasuke LINE alert + PENDING_REVIEW flag on failure; last probe 'BRIDGE OK' ~20s

features.name: Brain control web page
features.description: A simple local web page to switch the active brain and lock it, with live status.
features.notes: server.py serves GET / on :8720 (loopback only, never tunneled)

features.name: Registered QI project
features.description: Listed in the QI ecosystem registry with its own port block, services, tunnel, and integration contracts.
features.notes: id claude_voice, block 8720-8729, family_tier cousin, integrates_with qi_brain/nexus/maia

features.name: Reusable voice bridge
features.description: The speak/listen/realtime stack is offered to other QI projects (Maia, OpenClaw) as a shared voice feature.
features.notes: speak.py + listen.py + the realtime loop exposed to the ecosystem; not yet adopted elsewhere

features.name: Voice Dispatch to the QI Hive
features.description: Speak a work order and have the QI Hive execute it, then report back by voice — turning the assistant into a dispatch console.
features.notes: POST :9011/api/dispatch source=voice_*; needs a net-new executor + notification path

features.name: Natural low-latency voice (LiveKit)
features.description: Rebuild the voice loop on LiveKit for near-real-time, interruptible conversation.
features.notes: Phase 1; faster-whisper CUDA + Kokoro/Andrew + smart-turn endpointing

features.name: Zoom-like meetings with screen share
features.description: A real meeting interface where Claude is a participant who hears, speaks, and sees the shared screen.
features.notes: Phase 2; LiveKit meet UI then plugNmeet (screen/doc share, whiteboard, recording)
